model.name: rat liver in a normothermic machine perfusion

notes.body:
Machine perfusion of the liver (li) of the rat with 20 zone(s) in a circuit (pkpdsim.perfusion).
The rat liver in the circuit of the normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) flow study: the pump flow (1, 2 and 3 ml/min per g of liver in the groups of the study), the reservoir of the perfusate of 500 ml, the oxygenator ventilated with carbogen and the liver in 20 zones from periportal to pericentral, built with the machine perfusion library of pkpdsim (pkpdsim.perfusion).
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: the solubility of CO2 in plasma at 37 C, the textbook 0.0307 mmol/l/mmHg of the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation of plasma (0.0307/0.13332 kPa/mmHg); Christmas and Bassingthwaighte 2017 give the CO2 solubility of plasma and saline over the temperature, not read for this value; held at its 37 C value at every temperature, a model choice, the study is normothermic

parameter.name: solubility of oxygen at its reference temperature

body.p: derived: solubility of O2 in plasma at 37 C from Equation 4a of Christmas and Bassingthwaighte 2017 with rho_plasma = 1.020 g/ml and rho_water = 0.99332 g/ml (the authors call the plasma parameters tentative): 0.02149 ml gas/ml/atm, against 0.0214 in their Table 1 at 37 C (column assignment of the flattened table inferred), converted with 22.414 ml/mmol (STPD) and 101.325 kPa/atm. The perfusate of a machine perfusion without an oxygen carrier is closer to saline (0.02273 ml/ml/atm, 0.01001 mM/kPa), a model choice for the carrier.
Source:

ul.li: Christmas KM, Bassingthwaighte JB. Equations for O2 and CO2 solubilities in saline and plasma: combining temperature and density dependences. J Appl Physiol 122(5):1313-1320, 2017. doi:10.1152/japplphysiol.01124.2016

parameter.name: reference temperature of the solubility of oxygen

body.p: the temperature of the solubility and of its temperature coefficient, both evaluated at 37 C from Equation 4a of Christmas and Bassingthwaighte 2017; the solubility at another temperature is solubilityexp(temperature_coefficient(T - temperature)), a model choice which extrapolates the coefficient at 37 C
Source:

ul.li: Christmas KM, Bassingthwaighte JB. Equations for O2 and CO2 solubilities in saline and plasma: combining temperature and density dependences. J Appl Physiol 122(5):1313-1320, 2017. doi:10.1152/japplphysiol.01124.2016

parameter.name: temperature coefficient of the solubility of oxygen

body.p: derived: relative change of the solubility per K at 37 C, the central difference of Equation 4a of Christmas and Bassingthwaighte 2017 (plasma), i.e. a decrease of 1.3 % per K
Source:

ul.li: Christmas KM, Bassingthwaighte JB. Equations for O2 and CO2 solubilities in saline and plasma: combining temperature and density dependences. J Appl Physiol 122(5):1313-1320, 2017. doi:10.1152/japplphysiol.01124.2016

parameter.name: solubility of oxygen at the temperature
